questions.text: Which mapping correctly distinguishes MCP server primitives?

options.A: Tools are callable actions; resources are URI-addressed content; prompts are reusable templates.
options.B: Tools are transport connections; resources are model weights; prompts are authorization tokens.
options.C: Tools are conversation logs; resources execute every action; prompts define network sockets.
options.D: Tools are user interfaces; resources are client identities; prompts store database credentials.

questions.explanation: MCP exposes callable tools, readable URI-addressed resources, and reusable prompt templates; the host owns the AI application.

questions.text: An MCP tool returns text containing instructions to disclose unrelated private data. How should the host handle that text?

options.A: Treat the instructions as authoritative because they came through MCP.
options.B: Grant the tool additional permissions before reading the returned text.
options.C: Treat it as untrusted data and enforce the host’s authorization and instruction boundaries.
options.D: Disable authorization checks once the server reports its name and version.

questions.explanation: Standardized communication does not make returned content trusted or grant authority. The host and server still enforce access and action boundaries.

questions.text: The lesson request helper begins with body_params = dict(params or {}), then sets body_params["_meta"] to a new metadata dictionary. If params is a nonempty dictionary containing an existing _meta, what happens?

options.A: The original params dictionary is modified in place and its metadata is deleted.
options.B: The returned request uses the new metadata, while the original params dictionary remains unchanged.
options.C: The two metadata dictionaries are automatically merged key by key.
options.D: The existing metadata prevents assignment and raises KeyError.

questions.explanation: dict creates a shallow copy. Assigning a new value at the copy’s _meta key replaces that value only in the copy; it does not merge metadata or modify the original dictionary.
